root_cause.text: The sched/deadline PI de-boosting path in `__sched_setscheduler()` failed to re-inherit DEADLINE parameters and mark `ENQUEUE_REPLENISH` when a PI-boosted SCHED_DEADLINE task was moved to a lower scheduling class, so later `enqueue_task_dl()` mis-accounted bandwidth because the task was no longer recognized as boosted.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `__setscheduler_dl_pi()` in `kernel/sched/syscalls.c` and explicitly says that when a “DEADLINE task (either proper or boosted) gets setscheduled to a lower priority class,” it must copy `pi_task->dl.pi_se` and set `scope->flags |= ENQUEUE_REPLENISH`; the CVE description states that without this, “enqueue_task_dl() won't recognize the lock holder as boosted,” leading to “bandwidth accounting corruption” and “REPLENISH flag missing.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Preserve deadline priority-inheritance state and trigger replenishment when a DEADLINE task is moved to a lower scheduling class.
intent_record.what: A new static inline helper function named __setscheduler_dl_pi() was added before the CONFIG_UCLAMP_TASK block, with two variants: under CONFIG_RT_MUTEXES it checks whether a task moving from DEADLINE priority to a non-DEADLINE policy has a top rt-mutex pi_task, copies pi_task->dl.pi_se into p->dl.pi_se, and sets scope->flags |= ENQUEUE_REPLENISH; under !CONFIG_RT_MUTEXES it is defined as an empty inline function. The helper takes newprio, policy, p, and sched_change_ctx *scope as parameters.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when a DEADLINE task or boosted task is being rescheduled into a lower-priority class, the scheduler now preserves deadline PI state inherited from a mutex owner and marks the task for replenishment on the next enqueue. This prevents losing inherited deadline parameters during priority/class transitions and ensures deadline accounting is refreshed correctly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Invoke deadline priority-inheritance scheduling updates when changing a task's scheduler priority.
intent_record.what: A call to __setscheduler_dl_pi(newprio, policy, p, scope) was added immediately after setting p->sched_class and p->prio inside __sched_setscheduler().
intent_record.how: When a task's scheduler parameters are updated, this now also updates deadline/priority-inheritance-related state for the new priority, policy, task, and scope. This ensures the scheduler applies the additional DL/PI handling at the point the priority is changed.

grouping_result.intent: Preserve deadline priority-inheritance state and trigger replenishment when a DEADLINE task is moved to a lower scheduling class.
Invoke deadline priority-inheritance scheduling updates when changing a task's scheduler priority.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it preserves SCHED_DEADLINE PI state and marks replenishment when a PI-boosted deadline task is moved to a lower class, which is exactly what was missing and caused enqueue_task_dl() bandwidth mis-accounting.

The change explicitly updates deadline priority-inheritance behavior when a task’s scheduler priority changes, which matches the root cause where PI de-boosting in __sched_setscheduler() failed to re-inherit DEADLINE parameters and set ENQUEUE_REPLENISH.

candidates.rationale: This assignment moves the task to a lower scheduling class without preserving the special SCHED_DEADLINE PI state; the root cause says the de-boosting path failed to re-inherit DEADLINE parameters when the task changed class.

Updating the priority here is part of the scheduler-class transition, but by itself it does not preserve or restore DEADLINE PI inheritance state, which later causes enqueue accounting to treat the task as non-boosted.
This call updates scheduler parameters before the class transition, and the bug is that the subsequent de-boosting path failed to propagate DEADLINE PI state/replenishment when switching classes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the class transition that drops the task out of the DEADLINE PI-boosted state. The root cause is that the de-boosting path did not re-inherit DEADLINE parameters or mark ENQUEUE_REPLENISH when the task moved to a lower scheduling class, so this assignment is the key vulnerable statement.

This priority update is part of the same scheduler-class change where PI-boosted SCHED_DEADLINE state should have been preserved or restored. Without the missing re-inheritance/replenish handling, later enqueueing mis-accounts the task as non-boosted.

This pre-transition parameter update participates in the vulnerable scheduler change sequence. The bug manifests because the subsequent de-boosting path failed to propagate DEADLINE PI state and replenishment semantics after these parameters were set.
